subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Worm Gears: One-Way Power
description: A short lesson to help you apply Worm Gears: One-Way Power.

hook.text: A guitar tuning peg holds its position perfectly. You can turn it, but the string can't turn it back.

buildup.text: A worm gear pairs a screw-shaped worm with a toothed wheel. The worm drives the wheel but not the reverse.

discovery.text: This self-locking property comes from friction. The shallow angle of the worm prevents back-driving.

twist.text: Worm gears also achieve huge reduction ratios. One turn of the worm advances the wheel by just one tooth.

climax.text: Elevators use worm gears so the cab can't fall if power fails. Safety through geometry.

punchline.text: The worm gear turns easily one way. The other way, it locks.

quiz.question: Why can't a worm gear be back-driven?
options: The teeth are designed to break under reverse torque
Friction at the shallow worm angle prevents reverse motion
A mechanical brake automatically engages during back-drive
